passages.text: “Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look now and take note; search her squares. If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
God commands them to search their city.
He tells them to walk through the streets of Jerusalem.
He tells them to look carefully and pay attention.
He tells them to search in the public squares.
He asks them to look for one person.
He wants to find someone who does what is right.
He wants to find someone who seeks the truth.
God promises that if they find even one such person, He will forgive the whole city.
passages.original: שׁוֹטְט֞וּ בְּחוּצ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם וּרְאוּ־ נָ֤א וּדְעוּ֙ וּבַקְשׁ֣וּ בִרְחוֹבוֹתֶ֔יהָ אִם־ תִּמְצְא֣וּ אִ֔ישׁ אִם־ יֵ֛שׁ עֹשֶׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֱמוּנָ֑ה וְאֶסְלַ֖ח לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Although they say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ they are swearing falsely.”
passages.sermon:
The people say, “As surely as the LORD lives.”
They make this oath.
They do not speak the truth.
They swear falsely.
passages.original: וְאִ֥ם חַי־ יְהֹוָ֖ה יֹאמֵ֑רוּ לָכֵ֥ן לַשֶּׁ֖קֶר יִשָּׁבֵֽעוּ׃

passages.text: O LORD, do not Your eyes look for truth? You struck them, but they felt no pain. You finished them off, but they refused to accept discipline. They have made their faces harder than stone and refused to repent.
passages.sermon:
The Lord looks for truth.
The Lord seeks faithfulness.
The Lord struck the people.
The people felt no pain.
The Lord brought them to an end.
The people refused to accept discipline.
The people made their faces harder than stone.
The people refused to repent.
passages.original: יְהֹוָ֗ה עֵינֶיךָ֮ הֲל֣וֹא לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ הִכִּ֤יתָה אֹתָם֙ וְֽלֹא־ חָ֔לוּ כִּלִּיתָ֕ם מֵאֲנ֖וּ קַ֣חַת מוּסָ֑ר חִזְּק֤וּ פְנֵיהֶם֙ מִסֶּ֔לַע מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: Then I said, “They are only the poor; they have played the fool, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah spoke about the people of Judah.
He saw their sin and stubbornness.
He said, "These people are only the poor.
They are foolish.
They do not know the way of the LORD.
They do not know the justice of their God."
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַךְ־ דַּלִּ֖ים הֵ֑ם נוֹאֲל֕וּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדְעוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: I will go to the powerful and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” But they too, with one accord, had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.
passages.sermon:
The powerful people lead the nation.
They have authority and influence.
I will go to the powerful people.
I will speak to them.
They know the way of the LORD.
They understand the justice of their God.
But the powerful people acted together.
They broke the yoke.
They tore off the chains.
They rejected God’s rule.
passages.original: אֵֽלֲכָה־ לִּ֤י אֶל־ הַגְּדֹלִים֙ וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה אוֹתָ֔ם כִּ֣י הֵ֗מָּה יָדְעוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם אַ֣ךְ הֵ֤מָּה יַחְדָּו֙ שָׁ֣בְרוּ עֹ֔ל נִתְּק֖וּ מוֹסֵרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will ravage them. A leopard will lie in wait near their cities, and everyone who ventures out will be torn to pieces. For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Judah.
They have committed many rebellious acts.
They have done many unfaithful deeds.
Because of this, God will send judgment.
A lion from the forest will attack them.
A wolf from the desert will destroy them.
A leopard will wait near their cities.
Anyone who leaves the city will be torn apart.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֩ הִכָּ֨ם אַרְיֵ֜ה מִיַּ֗עַר זְאֵ֤ב עֲרָבוֹת֙ יְשָׁדְדֵ֔ם נָמֵ֤ר שֹׁקֵד֙ עַל־ עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם כָּל־ הַיּוֹצֵ֥א מֵהֵ֖נָּה יִטָּרֵ֑ף כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֔ם עָצְמ֖וּ מְשֻׁבוֹתֵיהֶם׃

passages.text: “Why should I forgive you? Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by gods that are not gods. I satisfied their needs, yet they committed adultery and assembled at the houses of prostitutes.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God asks, “Why should I forgive you?”
Your children have abandoned Me.
They have sworn oaths by false gods.
These gods are not real.
I gave your children everything they needed.
Still, they committed adultery.
They gathered together at the houses of prostitutes.
passages.original: אֵ֤י לָזֹאת֙ אֶסְלוֹחַ לָ֔ךְ בָּנַ֣יִךְ עֲזָב֔וּנִי וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ בְּלֹ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים וָאַשְׂבִּ֤עַ אוֹתָם֙ וַיִּנְאָ֔פוּ וּבֵ֥ית זוֹנָ֖ה יִתְגֹּדָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: They are well-fed, lusty stallions, each neighing after his neighbor’s wife.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel and Judah act like strong, healthy stallions.
They are well-fed.
They are full of desire.
Each man longs for his neighbor’s wife.
Each man chases after another man’s wife.
passages.original: סוּסִ֥ים מְיֻזָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁכִּ֣ים הָי֑וּ אִ֛ישׁ אֶל־ אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ יִצְהָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Should I not punish them for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD sees the sins of the people.
The people have turned away from the LORD.
The people have done evil things.
The LORD asks a question.
The LORD says, “Should I not punish them for these things?”
The LORD says, “Should I not avenge Myself on a nation like this?”
passages.original: הַֽעַל־ אֵ֥לֶּה לוֹא־ אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֑ה וְאִם֙ בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־ כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס

passages.text: Go up through her vineyards and ravage them, but do not finish them off. Strip off her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Israel and Judah.
They have been unfaithful to Him.
God commands others to go through their land.
He says, "Go up through her vineyards."
He says, "Ravage them."
He says, "Do not destroy them completely."
He says, "Strip off her branches."
He explains, "These branches do not belong to the LORD."
passages.original: עֲל֤וּ בְשָׁרוֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ וְשַׁחֵ֔תוּ וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל־ תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ הָסִ֙ירוּ֙ נְטִ֣ישׁוֹתֶ֔יהָ כִּ֛י ל֥וֹא לַיהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly unfaithful to Me,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD declares His judgment.
The house of Israel has been unfaithful to the LORD.
The house of Judah has also been unfaithful to the LORD.
Both Israel and Judah have betrayed the LORD completely.
passages.original: כִּי֩ בָג֨וֹד בָּגְד֜וּ בִּ֗י בֵּ֧ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וּבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They have lied about the LORD and said: “He will not do anything; harm will not come to us; we will not see sword or famine.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel and Judah lied about the LORD.
They said, “The LORD will not act.
No harm will come to us.
We will not see war.
We will not suffer from hunger.”
passages.original: כִּֽחֲשׁוּ֙ בַּיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹא־ ה֑וּא וְלֹא־ תָב֤וֹא עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ רָעָ֔ה וְחֶ֥רֶב וְרָעָ֖ב ל֥וֹא נִרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: The prophets are but wind, for the word is not in them. So let their own predictions befall them.”
passages.sermon:
The prophets speak empty words.
They have no true message from God.
God’s word is not in them.
Let their own words come back upon them.
Let what they say happen to them.
passages.original: וְהַנְּבִיאִים֙ יִֽהְי֣וּ לְר֔וּחַ וְהַדִּבֵּ֖ר אֵ֣ין בָּהֶ֑ם כֹּ֥ה יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה לָהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD God of Hosts says: “Because you have spoken this word, I will make My words a fire in your mouth and this people the wood it consumes.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
He speaks with authority and power.
He says this to the people.
You have spoken these words against Me.
Because of this, I will act.
I will put My words in your mouth.
My words will become like fire in your mouth.
These people are like wood.
The fire of My words will consume them.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת יַ֚עַן דַּבֶּרְכֶ֔ם אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹתֵן֩ דְּבָרַ֨י בְּפִ֜יךָ לְאֵ֗שׁ וְהָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה עֵצִ֖ים וַאֲכָלָֽתַם׃

passages.text: Behold, I am bringing a distant nation against you, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD. “It is an established nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Hosts.
The LORD speaks to the house of Israel.
The LORD says, “I am bringing a nation against you.
This nation comes from far away.
This nation is strong.
This nation is ancient.
You do not know their language.
You do not understand what they say.”
passages.original: הִנְנִ֣י מֵבִיא֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם גּ֧וֹי מִמֶּרְחָ֛ק בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֑ה גּ֣וֹי׀ אֵיתָ֣ן ה֗וּא גּ֤וֹי מֵעוֹלָם֙ ה֔וּא גּ֚וֹי לֹא־ תֵדַ֣ע לְשֹׁנ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁמַ֖ע מַה־ יְדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Their quivers are like open graves; they are all mighty men.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the nation He is bringing against Israel.
This nation is strong.
All its men are mighty warriors.
Their quivers are like open graves.
Their weapons bring death.
passages.original: אַשְׁפָּת֖וֹ כְּקֶ֣בֶר פָּת֑וּחַ כֻּלָּ֖ם גִּבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: They will devour your harvest and food; they will consume your sons and daughters; they will eat up your flocks and herds; they will feed on your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will destroy the fortified cities in which you trust.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of Israel.
God says a distant nation will come against you.
This nation will take your harvest.
They will eat your food.
They will consume your sons.
They will consume your daughters.
They will eat your flocks.
They will eat your herds.
They will feed on your vines.
They will feed on your fig trees.
They will destroy your fortified cities with the sword.
You trust in these cities.
They will not protect you.
passages.original: וְאָכַ֨ל קְצִֽירְךָ֜ וְלַחְמֶ֗ךָ יֹאכְלוּ֙ בָּנֶ֣יךָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יךָ יֹאכַ֤ל צֹאנְךָ֙ וּבְקָרֶ֔ךָ יֹאכַ֥ל גַּפְנְךָ֖ וּתְאֵנָתֶ֑ךָ יְרֹשֵׁ֞שׁ עָרֵ֣י מִבְצָרֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בָּהֵ֖נָּה בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: “Yet even in those days,” declares the LORD, “I will not make a full end of you.
passages.sermon: The LORD speaks to the people of Judah and Israel.\r\nHe says, “Even in those days of trouble, I will not destroy you completely.\r\nI will not bring a total end to you.”
passages.original: וְגַ֛ם בַּיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵ֖מָּה נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֑ה לֹֽא־ אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם כָּלָֽה׃

passages.text: And when the people ask, ‘For what offense has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ You are to tell them, ‘Just as you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
He speaks to the people of Israel.
He says, “You will ask, ‘Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’
You will wonder what offense caused this.
You must answer them.
You abandoned the LORD.
You served foreign gods in your own land.
In the same way, you will serve foreigners.
You will serve them in a land that does not belong to you.”
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ תַּ֣חַת מֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֨ה יְהֹוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ לָ֖נוּ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עֲזַבְתֶּ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ וַתַּעַבְד֞וּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י נֵכָר֙ בְּאַרְצְכֶ֔ם כֵּ֚ן תַּעַבְד֣וּ זָרִ֔ים בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א לָכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Declare this in the house of Jacob and proclaim it in Judah: “Hear this, O foolish and senseless people, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel and Judah.
He told them to declare a message in the house of Jacob.
He told them to proclaim it in Judah.
He said, "Listen to this, you foolish and senseless people.
You have eyes, but you do not see.
You have ears, but you do not hear."
passages.original: הַגִּ֥ידוּ זֹ֖את בְּבֵ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ בִיהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל וְאֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב עֵינַ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ אָזְנַ֥יִם לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Do you not fear Me?” declares the LORD. “Do you not tremble before Me, the One who set the sand as the boundary for the sea, an enduring barrier it cannot cross? The waves surge, but they cannot prevail. They roar but cannot cross it.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD asks a question.
The LORD says, "Do you not fear Me?"
The LORD says, "Do you not tremble before Me?"
The LORD set the sand as a boundary for the sea.
This boundary is an everlasting rule.
The sea cannot cross this boundary.
The waves of the sea surge.
The waves cannot overcome the boundary.
The waves roar.
The waves cannot cross the boundary.
passages.original: הַאוֹתִ֨י לֹא־ תִירָ֜אוּ נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֗ה אִ֤ם מִפָּנַי֙ לֹ֣א תָחִ֔ילוּ אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֤מְתִּי חוֹל֙ גְּב֣וּל לַיָּ֔ם חָק־ עוֹלָ֖ם וְלֹ֣א יַעַבְרֶ֑נְהוּ וַיִּֽתְגָּעֲשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יוּכָ֔לוּ וְהָמ֥וּ גַלָּ֖יו וְלֹ֥א יַעַבְרֻֽנְהוּ׃

passages.text: But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned aside and gone away.
passages.sermon:
These people belong to the house of Jacob and Judah.
They have stubborn hearts.
They have rebellious hearts.
They turned aside from the right way.
They went away from God.
passages.original: וְלָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ הָיָ֔ה לֵ֖ב סוֹרֵ֣ר וּמוֹרֶ֑ה סָ֖רוּ וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: They have not said in their hearts, ‘Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rains, both autumn and spring, in season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.’
passages.sermon:
The people have not said in their hearts, "Let us fear the LORD our God."
The LORD is our God.
The LORD gives rain.
He gives autumn rain.
He gives spring rain.
He gives rain at the right time.
He keeps the weeks of harvest for us.
He makes sure we have our harvest at the appointed time.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָמְר֣וּ בִלְבָבָ֗ם נִ֤ירָא נָא֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הַנֹּתֵ֗ן גֶּ֛שֶׁם וְיֹרֶה וּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ בְּעִתּ֑וֹ שְׁבֻע֛וֹת חֻקּ֥וֹת קָצִ֖יר יִשְׁמָר־ לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
The people have sinned.
Their iniquities have turned good things away from them.
Their sins have kept blessings from them.
God’s bounty does not reach them because of their wrongdoing.
passages.original: עֲוֺנוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם הִטּוּ־ אֵ֑לֶּה וְחַטֹּ֣אותֵיכֶ֔ם מָנְע֥וּ הַטּ֖וֹב מִכֶּֽם׃

passages.text: For among My people are wicked men; they watch like fowlers lying in wait; they set a trap to catch men.
passages.sermon:
Among my people are wicked men.
These men act with evil intent.
They watch carefully.
They wait like hunters who catch birds.
They set traps.
They try to catch other people in their traps.
passages.original: כִּי־ נִמְצְא֥וּ בְעַמִּ֖י רְשָׁעִ֑ים יָשׁוּר֙ כְּשַׁ֣ךְ יְקוּשִׁ֔ים הִצִּ֥יבוּ מַשְׁחִ֖ית אֲנָשִׁ֥ים יִלְכֹּֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Like cages full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become powerful and rich.
passages.sermon:
The people are wicked.
Their houses are full of deceit.
Their houses are like cages full of birds.
They have become powerful.
They have become rich.
passages.original: כִּכְלוּב֙ מָ֣לֵא ע֔וֹף כֵּ֥ן בָּתֵּיהֶ֖ם מְלֵאִ֣ים מִרְמָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּ֥ן גָּדְל֖וּ וַֽיַּעֲשִֽׁירוּ׃

passages.text: They have grown fat and sleek, and have excelled in the deeds of the wicked. They have not taken up the cause of the fatherless, that they might prosper; nor have they defended the rights of the needy.
passages.sermon:
Wicked men live among God's people.
These men have grown fat.
They have become sleek.
They do many evil deeds.
They do not defend the fatherless.
They do not help orphans succeed.
They do not judge the cause of the needy.
They do not defend the rights of the poor.
passages.original: שָׁמְנ֣וּ עָשְׁת֗וּ גַּ֚ם עָֽבְר֣וּ דִבְרֵי־ רָ֔ע דִּ֣ין לֹא־ דָ֔נוּ דִּ֥ין יָת֖וֹם וְיַצְלִ֑יחוּ וּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לֹ֥א שָׁפָֽטוּ׃

passages.text: Should I not punish them for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD sees the evil deeds of the people.
The LORD asks a question.
The LORD says, “Should I not punish them for these things?”
The LORD says, “Should I not take revenge on a nation like this?”
passages.original: הַֽעַל־ אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא־ אֶפְקֹ֖ד נְאֻם־ יְהֹוָ֑ה אִ֚ם בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־ כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס

passages.text: A horrible and shocking thing has happened in the land.
passages.sermon: A horrible thing has happened in the land.\r\nA shocking thing has happened in the land.
passages.original: שַׁמָּה֙ וְשַׁ֣עֲרוּרָ֔ה נִהְיְתָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority. My people love it so, but what will you do in the end?
passages.sermon:
The prophets speak lies.
The priests rule by their own power.
The people of Israel love these things.
But what will you do when the end comes?
passages.original: הַנְּבִיאִ֞ים נִבְּא֣וּ־ בַשֶּׁ֗קֶר וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ יִרְדּ֣וּ עַל־ יְדֵיהֶ֔ם וְעַמִּ֖י אָ֣הֲבוּ כֵ֑ן וּמַֽה־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ לְאַחֲרִיתָֽהּ׃
